thread:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 — canary error-rate spike for api-server in prod-us-west. 5xx increased from ~0.12% to 4.3% over 6m. Source: canary rollout window 2026-03-15T21:34Z. Affected route: /v1/generate. Paging eng-oncall and eng-sre. Dashboard: https://redwood.monitoring/d/abc123/canary?from=now-15m

Anya (oncall): i'm on it, grabbing logs and kube state. @here

Sam L: which deployment/helm release was rolled?

Jordan R: canary was pushed via the weekly deploy pipeline — release id 2026-03-15-canary. Quick check: pods are running image tag `canary-latest` which resolved to a different digest than the build we validated. Looks like mutable tag drift. Pasting `kubectl describe pod` snippet below:
```
Name: api-server-5f9c7b6b9f-ndk2
Image: gcr.io/redwood/api-server:canary-latest
Image ID: docker-pullable://gcr.io/redwood/api-server@sha256:deadbeef...
State: Running
Last Termination: CrashLoopBackOff ->  rpc error: code = Unknown desc = incompatible binary version
```

CI Bot: Build pipeline 20260315.1733 succeeded and published `gcr.io/redwood/api-server:canary-latest` -> digest sha256:abc123 (intended). However, registry shows previous tag float for same name pointing at sha256:deadbeef due to manual push in the registry proxy around 21:28Z.

Kelly (SRE): this is a mutable-tag / cache-poisoning symptom. immediate mitigation: disable canary routing in prod (feature-flag kill-switch) and rollback the canary deployment. i'll toggle the flag now.

Kelly (SRE): ffcli toggle enable_canary_routing --env prod --off  -> response: OK

Paul - infra: starting rollback of the canary release to stable revision.
```bash
kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-server --namespace=prod --to-revision=10
kubectl set image deployment/api-server api-server=gcr.io/redwood/api-server@sha256:stable123 --namespace=prod
```

Anya (oncall): rollback in progress. watching metrics...

(5 minutes later)
Anya (oncall): error rate fell back to ~0.25% within 4m after rollback and FF toggle. 5xx volume returning to baseline.

Sam L: customer impact? which tenants hit errors?

Anya (oncall): initial query shows ~8 Dedicated tenants in us-west saw elevated 5xx for ~6 minutes; a couple of high-volume hosted customers saw transient failures (aggregate ~1.2k failed requests). Sending list to CS.

Jordan R: preliminary root cause: helm values used mutable tag `canary-latest` for prod canary; registry had out-of-band push that changed what that tag pointed to (mutable tag drift). pipeline didn't validate final digest at deployment time. Also our registry proxy cached an older manifest leading to mismatch.

CI Bot: queued enforcement job: `ci/enforce-image-digest` will block deploys using mutable tags for prod and add a preflight digest-check step. Also scheduled registry GC and manifest integrity scan.

Kelly (SRE): followups to create: (1) fail-build-on-mutable-tag-for-prod (2) patch helm charts to require digest pinning or CI substitution (3) add registry tag-mutation monitor and alert (4) postmortem + customer comms.

Paul - infra: filed a short incident ticket and linked this thread to incidents channel: https://slack.com/app_redirect?channel=incidents&message=1993456789. Also created internal ticket INFRA-4521 to pin production charts.

Sam L: please notify CS & account ops with impacted tenant list and timeframe. cc @support-leads

Anya (oncall): handing over to Kelly for follow-up and postmortem. Kelly, you're primary for the next 12h on this. I'll add notes to the incident doc and attach kube/registry artifacts.

Kelly (SRE): acknowledged, taking over. I'll coordinate postmortem, assign owners, and add a remediation timeline.

Anya (oncall): closing pager for now — system stabilized. Will raise a formal postmortem and follow-ups in eng-infra. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
